item.title: [infoq] 企业 AI 越用越复杂，如何用一个 Gateway 管好模型、Agent 和成本？｜ 技术趋势
item.description: Snowflake's Cortex AI Gateway has entered public preview, positioned as a control plane between AI clients and the enterprise systems they reach, offering governed model inference, dynamic model routing, MCP and tool governance, observability, guardrails and cost attribution through a single endpoint. The article argues that fragmentation in enterprise AI stacks comes from a missing control layer rather than a shortage of tools, and targets platform teams responsible for governance and spend.

item.description: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

item.description: A V2EX developer posting as 耶格尔 launched a browser-based video downloader that requires no app install: paste a link, the server parses it, and the file downloads. It covers YouTube, Bilibili, Weibo, Xiaohongshu, X and Instagram, and accepts whole share texts by pulling the URL out automatically. The tool is free and the author is soliciting feedback; the post also claims support for 91 and Pornhub.

item.title: [v2ex] [输入法] 搜狗输入法是限制词库导出了吗？
item.description: A V2EX user trying to migrate years of accumulated Sogou IME vocabulary to other input methods found the exported bin file was only about 400KB, and converting it with the 深蓝 tool yielded just a few dozen entries, even though Sogou's phone-side sync shows roughly 30,000 words. Installing older Sogou versions gave the same result, prompting him to suspect the export is deliberately capped and to ask whether others are seeing this too.

item.title: [infoq] 面向 Qwen 系列模型线性注意力的高性能优化实践
item.description: This write-up follows a talk by Alibaba Qwen team engineer Zhang Chengruidong at AICon 2026 Shenzhen on FlashQLA, a GPU operator library for GDN (Gated Delta Network) linear attention. It starts from the matrix-multiplication argument that takes linear attention from O(N²d) to O(Nd²), then covers sequence parallelism, exploiting sliding-window properties, hardware-friendly algebraic rewrites and warp specialization, closing with benchmarks and ecosystem integration.

item.description: Researchers from Meta, MIT and the University of Washington propose Context Language Model, which treats context as a freely rewritable file: the model deletes irrelevant turns, keeps key facts and tracks progress instead of relying on summarization or retrieval. Zero-shot it lifts BrowseComp-Plus accuracy by 11.4% with 21.5% fewer FLOPs, and an RL-trained Qwen3.5-9B climbs from 28.8% to 42.5% on the same benchmark.

item.title: [hackernews] eMudhra intermediate CA compromise
item.description: A Mozilla security blog post and Bugzilla bug 2083449 cover a compromise of an intermediate CA run by eMudhra. When an intermediate certificate authority is compromised, every certificate it issued has to be treated as suspect, which bears directly on the public trust chain browsers rely on. The linked pages aren't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [infoq] 决策模型也有专用推理引擎了：StartLux 开源 Prism，单卡最高提速 5.3 倍
item.description: StartLux has open-sourced Prism, an inference engine built specifically for its StartLux-Decision model. On a single NVIDIA H200 running the 27B model, it claims 1.2x to 5.3x the speed of vLLM, cutting a three-question task on one document from 92.9ms to 17.4ms. Because decision models only score a handful of candidate options rather than generate full text, Prism skips whole-vocabulary output and returns bit-identical results regardless of batching; accuracy was 92.94% against 92.97% in BF16.

item.description: Huawei's Xiaoyi Work, built with openJiuwen and in beta since September, now runs on HarmonyOS and Windows, comes preinstalled on HarmonyOS PCs, and offers new users 1000 AI credits for 31 days. InfoQ tested it on three editorial tasks: adapting one article into multi-platform copy, scheduling a daily embodied-AI briefing, and turning a story into a research deck. The review focuses on whether outputs stay editable and where humans must step in.

item.title: [infoq] Xcode 27.2 推出对智能体友好、有效减少合并冲突的 JSON 项目配置格式
item.description: Apple has introduced a JSON-based project format in Xcode 27.2, replacing the long-standing property-list project.pbxproj with a project.xcproj file. Apple also open-sourced the xcode-project-format spec and a Swift package for encoding and decoding it, so tooling can walk targets, build settings and dependencies. item.description: NVIDIA has open-sourced OpenShell, described as a safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents, Apache-2.0 licensed and published on PyPI. The 0.1.x line adds a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface and new APIs. It targets teams that need to run many agents inside an isolated, private environment.

item.title: [hackernews] Eight Bits of Trust: eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
item.description: Scott Helme recovered the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates straight from their public certificates in under a second, because the keys were tiny integers such as 4, 56 and 115. The compromise was reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on 17 October; Chrome shipped a CRLSet block that evening and Firefox followed hours later through OneCRL.

item.description: Developer Sammy Hajhamid released ns2jb, a software-only tethered jailbreak for the Switch 2 that works on the current 23.0.1 firmware and runs arbitrary native code as an ordinary sysmodule or as the built-in fs sysmodule. He calls it the first such exploit for the console, enabling homebrew, game modding, save backups and MMIO access to most peripherals; the demo mods Mario Kart World using Codex.

item.description: Starting from a single satellite screenshot handed over by a client, the author rebuilt a 3D integrated energy station with Three.js and Blender: reverse-engineering the design camera from the image, scripting the modeling, baking a night scene in Cycles, then adding a truck reversing into a bay and an operations simulation, with a pixel-by-pixel overlay to check fidelity. Useful for front-end developers working on Web 3D visualization, digital twins, or reconstructing scenes from reference imag

item.title: [juejin] 用了一个月 WorkBuddy，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A heavy GPT user of more than two years, who writes proposals, edits copy and sorts materials with it, explains that he has long relied on third-party relay APIs because of network constraints, and now shares what a month of using WorkBuddy actually felt like. Devs who also reach models through relay endpoints will find this kind of long-term, hands-on account more useful than launch-day benchmarks.

item.title: [github_trending] SnailSploit/Claude-Red
item.description: Claude-Red is a curated offensive security library from SnailSploit, shipping 78 structured SKILL.md files across 23 categories that prime Claude with expert-level red team methodology. Drop them into the Claude skills system and the model operates as a context-aware red team operator. It is MIT licensed, aimed at pentesters and red teamers who want reusable, drop-in skill definitions rather than ad-hoc prompts.

item.title: [juejin] 太猛了，一个月干到15W+，给大家推荐一个最近爆火的开源逆向工具：REA
item.description: REA is an open-source reverse engineering tool whose repository was only created this April, yet it has climbed past 150,000 stars in little more than a month. The article walks through what the project is and how to get started with it. Useful for anyone doing reverse engineering, security analysis, or binary inspection who wants a quick orientation before trying it out.

item.title: [juejin] 老干妈靠AI闷赚54亿，你的AI还在写文案？
item.description: Starting from the claim that Lao Gan Ma quietly earned 5.4 billion through AI, the piece tallies the cost of repetitive back-office work: site managers spend an hour a day filling Excel sheets, accountants spend another hour keying the data into finance software, and five full-time accountants exist just for that, costing hundreds of thousands a year in salaries. The argument is that AI belongs in these process-heavy roles, not just in copywriting.

item.title: [github_trending] OpenBMB/VoxCPM
item.description: OpenBMB has released VoxCPM2, a tokenizer-free TTS model built for multilingual speech generation, creative voice design, and high-fidelity voice cloning. Weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with a hosted demo space, ReadTheDocs documentation, and an arXiv paper alongside. Teams building speech synthesis or dubbing features can try it without waiting for a hosted API.

item.title: [github_trending] nodejs/node
item.description: nodejs/node is the main repository for Node.js, the open-source cross-platform JavaScript runtime. Its README lays out the project's open governance, with a Technical Steering Committee (TSC) making decisions and the OpenJS Foundation providing support, plus Current, LTS and Nightly release channels and instructions for verifying binaries. Developers checking release cadence, build steps, security process or how to contribute will find the details there.
